title: Prompt versioning and LLMOps
summary: Treat the prompt, model version, parameters, tools and retrieval settings as one release unit: version it, gate it on evals, canary it and keep a pinned bundle to roll back to.
useIf: A prompt or model change can reach real users and you need to know which combination produced which behaviour.
avoidIf: You are prototyping with a single user. Heavy release machinery before a golden set exists only slows you down.

explain.md: Model behaviour depends on a **combination**: model version, prompt, configuration, orchestration logic, tools and retrieval. The Azure Architecture Center says all of these changes must be tested and the tested combination **pinned together** in production. A router can then support blue-green, A/B and traffic mirroring without mixing untested combinations, and logs should carry enough metadata to correlate behaviour with prompt, config, model and retrieval versions [[r10]]. OpenAI gives the same advice: pin to a dated model snapshot and build evals that measure prompt behaviour when you iterate or upgrade [[tr3]].

explain.title: A release path for a prompt change

steps.title: Change
steps.md: Edit the prompt, model, config, tool or retrieval setting in version control.

steps.title: Offline gate
steps.md: Run the golden set against the new bundle. Block on regressions.

steps.title: Mirror
steps.md: Copy live traffic to the candidate and compare without serving it.

steps.title: Canary
steps.md: Serve a small slice. Watch quality, latency, cost and refusals.

steps.title: Promote and pin
steps.md: Pin the tested bundle and log its versions on every request.

steps.title: Roll back
steps.md: Re-point to the last pinned bundle if metrics breach a threshold.

explain.md: **Where prompts live** is a real decision. OpenAI advises, as of 2026-10-13, keeping production prompts in application code: typed inputs, code review, tests and your normal deployment process, with feature flags or config for staged rollouts. Its reusable prompt objects are being deprecated: creation is de-emphasized from 2026-06-03 and `v1/prompts` is scheduled to shut down on 2026-11-30 [[tr3]]. Do not make a vendor-hosted prompt store or eval tool your only system of record. The dataset-backed prompt optimizer and Evals platform are read-only for existing users on 2026-10-31 with shutdown scheduled for 2026-11-30 [[r11]].

explain.title: Retirement is a release event
explain.md: Retired model deployments return HTTP errors. Deprecated deployments accept no new deployments but keep working until retirement [[r10]]. Put retirement dates in your release calendar and canary the replacement model with the pinned prompt before the cutoff.

whereToUse: Any production assistant or agent where a prompt edit can change answers for users
Teams where several people edit prompts, tools or retrieval settings
Model upgrades and deprecations that force a swap on a deadline
Regulated or audited apps that must reproduce what a user saw
Agent platforms where instructions are versioned objects that can be promoted

use: Every change to prompt, model, config, tools or retrieval goes through an eval gate
You can log versions on each request for correlation
You need a one-step rollback to a known-good bundle
avoid: Editing the live prompt in a console with no review or eval
Using a floating model alias such as 'latest' in production
Letting a vendor-hosted prompt store be the only copy
flips: Non-engineers must edit prompts: add a reviewed config store with the same eval gate
Traffic is tiny: skip shadow and canary, but keep the offline gate and pinning
A deadline-driven model retirement: shadow and canary the replacement first

pitfalls.symptom: Behaviour changes after a harmless prompt tweak
pitfalls.cause: An untested combination of prompt, model, config or retrieval reached production
pitfalls.fix: Gate every change on the offline eval and deploy only pinned bundles with versions logged per request.

pitfalls.symptom: Eval scores stay green but users complain
pitfalls.cause: The golden set is stale or tuned to the prompt
pitfalls.fix: Refresh it from real traces, hold out a test slice and watch live quality, refusal and cost metrics in the canary.

pitfalls.symptom: Requests start failing with HTTP errors one morning
pitfalls.fix: Track retirement dates, canary the replacement ahead of time and keep the previous bundle for rollback while it still exists.

scenarios.title: Small team, one prompt, weekly edits
scenarios.situation: Three engineers maintain one assistant. The prompt changes weekly. A golden set of 200 cases exists. Traffic is modest.
unknowns: Does anyone outside engineering edit the prompt?
How costly is a bad answer?
scenarios.question: Where does the prompt live and how does it ship?

options.name: A shared document pasted into config by hand
options.tradeoff: No automated gate, so regressions reach users until someone notices.

options.name: A vendor-hosted prompt object edited in a console
options.why: OpenAI is deprecating reusable prompt objects and `v1/prompts` shuts down on 2026-11-30.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable only for a short-lived prototype that will be migrated.

options.name: In Git with a CI eval gate and a feature flag for rollout
options.why: Matches OpenAI's advice to version prompts in code, and the gate blocks regressions cheaply.
options.tradeoff: Releasing a prompt change needs a deploy or a flag flip.

flips.if: A policy team must edit wording daily
flips.then: Move to a reviewed config store that triggers the same eval gate.

flips.if: Traffic grows and quality is revenue-critical
flips.then: Add shadow traffic and a canary stage.

scenarios.takeaway: For engineer-owned prompts, code review plus an eval gate is the cheapest safe release path.

scenarios.title: Model deprecation on a deadline
scenarios.situation: A high-traffic assistant runs on a model whose retirement date is eight weeks away. The replacement behaves differently on refusals and formatting.
unknowns: How large is the golden set for format-sensitive cases?
scenarios.question: How do you migrate?

options.name: Switch the alias to the new model and watch dashboards
options.why: It ships an untested combination to everyone and rollback depends on the old model still existing.
options.tradeoff: Only acceptable for low-risk internal tools with instant rollback.

options.name: Pin a candidate bundle, run the offline gate, mirror traffic, then canary
options.why: Each stage exposes a different kind of regression before most users see it.
options.tradeoff: Takes calendar time and needs mirroring plus metrics for refusals and format validity.

options.name: Offline eval only, then cut over
options.why: Catches many regressions at low cost.
options.tradeoff: Offline sets miss live traffic quirks, so incidents surface in production.

flips.if: The replacement is the same family and behaviour is near-identical
flips.then: A short canary may be enough.
Compress shadow time and widen alerts, but keep the canary.

scenarios.takeaway: Treat retirement dates as release deadlines and de-risk the swap in stages.

quiz.q: Order the safe release path for a prompt change.
quiz.explain: Gate on the golden set first, then compare on live traffic without serving, then serve a small slice, then promote the tested bundle and pin it.

quiz.q: What does a deprecated Azure model deployment do before retirement?
options: Accepts no new deployments but keeps working until retirement
Returns HTTP errors immediately, exactly like a retired deployment
Switches to the newest model automatically
quiz.explain: Deprecated deployments keep working until retirement but cannot be newly deployed. Retired deployments return HTTP errors, and nothing switches models automatically.

quiz.q: Why avoid a floating 'latest' model alias in production?
options: It always costs more per token than a pinned snapshot
It can change behaviour without a tested bundle
quiz.explain: A floating alias can move to a different snapshot, so the tested combination is no longer what runs. It does not inherently cost more, block logging or disable caching.

flashcards.front: What should be pinned together in production?
flashcards.back: Model version, prompt, configuration, orchestration logic and retrieval settings, because the tested combination is the release unit.

flashcards.front: When does OpenAI's `v1/prompts` reusable prompt API shut down?
flashcards.back: Scheduled for 2026-11-30. OpenAI advises versioning prompts in application code instead.

flashcards.front: What changes for the OpenAI Evals platform and dataset-backed prompt optimizer on 2026-10-31?
flashcards.back: They become read-only for existing users, with shutdown scheduled for 2026-11-30.
